stages.name: Public and private sector organisations
stages.title: Public and private sector organisations
stages.sub: After this, the student can tell whether an organisation belongs to the public or private sector and why that matters.

steps.q: A hospital is run and paid for by the government, using taxpayers' money, to provide free healthcare. Who owns it?
steps.right: The government, on behalf of everyone
steps.wrong: A group of shareholders who invested money
steps.hint: Think about where the money to run the hospital actually comes from.
steps.pre: An organisation owned and funded by the government to provide a service is in the

steps.q: A local bakery is owned by a family, who put in their own savings and keep any profit it makes. Who owns it?
steps.right: The family who set it up
steps.hint: Who put the money in, and who gets to keep what is left over?
steps.pre: An organisation owned by individuals aiming to make a profit is in the

steps.q: The hospital's money comes from taxes collected from everyone, while the bakery's money came from the family's own savings. Are these two organisations funded in the same way?
steps.right: No, they come from different sources
steps.wrong: Yes, both rely on the same source of money
steps.hint: One is funded by the state, the other by private individuals.

steps.q: The bakery closes early on a quiet Tuesday because it wasn't worth the cost of staying open. Could the hospital shut for the day for the same reason?
steps.right: No, it still has to provide the service
steps.wrong: Yes, if running it costs more than it earns
steps.hint: What is each organisation ultimately trying to achieve: money left over, or a service delivered regardless?

steps.q: Given that they differ in who owns and funds them, and in whether they aim for profit or for providing a service regardless of cost, are these two types of organisation the same kind of thing?
steps.wrong: Yes, they work in much the same way
steps.hint: Put ownership and aim together: do they point to one category of organisation, or two separate ones?
